title: Read the primary mouse button, not the physical left one, to end a Tumbler drag
body:
## Summary
table_os::left_mouse_pressed() asks GetAsyncKeyState(VK_LBUTTON), which reports the PHYSICAL left button; with swapped buttons the 1 s tick ends every drag mid-move.

## Description
crates/table-os/src/windows_native.rs:216-219 reads GetAsyncKeyState(1). Microsoft documents that GetAsyncKeyState checks physical buttons, not the logical mapping (recalled; mark UNVERIFIED until checked). apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/native/events.rs:110 calls tumbler_snap whenever dragging && !left_mouse_pressed(). A left-handed owner (SM_SWAPBUTTON) drags with the physical right button, so within a second the shell snaps and repositions the Tumbler while the OS move loop is still running. Fixed: pick VK_RBUTTON when GetSystemMetrics(SM_SWAPBUTTON) != 0 (native-shell-integration / layout-resolved-input-synthesis: resolve at the layer the target matches on).

## Flow
- owner with swapped buttons presses on the Tumbler -> tumbler_drag sets dragging and starts the OS move
- next 1 s tick: left_mouse_pressed() false -> tumbler_snap -> set_form moves the window mid-drag
- fix: pure primary_button_vk(swapped) + GetSystemMetrics(SM_SWAPBUTTON) inside the reader (rename primary_button_pressed)

## Expected impact
Left-handed owners can drag the Tumbler; right-handed behaviour unchanged. Could break if the metric is read wrong, so the pure mapping gets a unit test.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a drag with swapped mouse buttons is not cut short
Before: drag cut within ~1 s for swapped-button users (walked: events.rs:110 + windows_native.rs:218)
After: drag ends only on primary-button release
Method: simulation - needs a Windows session with swapped buttons; no in-tree instrument drives a real OS drag
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: unit test on a pure primary_button_vk(swapped: bool) mapping, plus an #[ignore] test that calls SwapMouseButton(TRUE), asserts the reader picks VK_RBUTTON, and restores; manual drag with the primary button set to right

title: Show a startup failure to the owner instead of printing to a console that does not exist
body:
## Summary
In a release build main.rs prints a failed start with eprintln under windows_subsystem=windows, so the app silently never appears.

## Description
apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs:1 sets windows_subsystem = "windows" in release; main.rs:4-6 reports any run() error with eprintln!. run() fails on a ledger that will not open, a vault/keyring error, engine attachment or MCP attachment (native.rs setup, the map_err(io::Error::other(...)) chain). The owner double-clicks and nothing happens, with no message. Same family: native/events.rs notify_once eprintln for a failed decision toast, invisible in release. Fixed: a table-os fatal_message(text) (MessageBoxW, plain words) called from main on Err.

## Flow
- release build, wallet.sqlite unreadable -> setup returns Err
- main.rs eprintln -> no console -> nothing on screen
- fix: table_os::fatal_message("The Table could not start: ...") before exit

## Expected impact
Owners see why the wallet did not start; no change on success. The new unsafe call is one MessageBoxW.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a failed start is visible
Before: 0 of 4 setup failure kinds visible in a release build (walked)
After: 4 of 4 shown in a native message box
Method: simulation - needs a release build and a forced setup failure; not runnable in a round
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: release build with APPDATA pointed at a read-only directory (or a corrupt wallet.sqlite): Before no window and no dialog, After a message box naming the failure; plus a unit test on the pure message text

title: Remove the notification plugin the shell initialises and never uses
body:
## Summary
tauri-plugin-notification is a dependency and is registered at startup, but nothing calls it: toasts go through tauri-winrt-notification directly.

## Description
apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/native.rs (.plugin(tauri_plugin_notification::init())) and apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml:31. Consumers: grep NotificationExt / .notification( in apps/desktop/src-tauri/src -> 0; no notification:* permission in any capability file; apps/desktop/client/src never imports @tauri-apps/plugin-notification (0 hits). show_toast in native/events.rs uses tauri_winrt_notification::Toast. AGENTS: keep dependencies few. Fixed: drop the plugin line and the Cargo entry; Cargo.lock shrinks.

## Flow
- cargo tree -p table-desktop counts the plugin's subtree
- remove the .plugin line and Cargo.toml:31
- re-run clippy/test and show one decision toast manually

## Expected impact
Smaller build and dependency surface; toasts unchanged because they never used the plugin. Could break toasts only if the plugin's init had a side effect the WinRT path relied on.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one unused runtime dependency removed
Before: 1 plugin initialised with 0 consumers (grep)
After: 0
Method: probe - grep for consumers; Cargo.lock is a shared surface, so not built in-round
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/native.rs:183 (.plugin(tauri_plugin_notification::init()))
apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml:31
grep NotificationExt|.notification( apps/desktop/src-tauri/src -> 0
grep plugin-notification apps/desktop/client/src -> 0
instrument: cargo tree -p table-desktop -e normal line count before/after; clippy/test -p table-desktop green; one manual decision toast in a debug run

title: Refuse new-window requests from every webview, not only navigation
body:
## Summary
Each window installs on_navigation, but no builder handles new-window requests (window.open, target=_blank), whose default WebView2 behaviour no test pins.

## Description
apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/native.rs (main and tumbler builders) and native/routing.rs:65-78 (approval) set .on_navigation(navigation::permits) and nothing for new windows. navigation.rs guards in-place navigation only. If WebView2 opens a popup for window.open, that popup is not a Tauri window, has no navigation guard and loads any URL; main renders counterparty text (as text). Tauri 2.12 default unverified here. Fixed: an on_new_window handler that denies on all three builders, pinned by extending every_window_is_built_with_the_navigation_guard.

## Flow
- debug build, devtools in main: window.open('https://example.com')
- observe: popup window / system browser / nothing
- fix: .on_new_window(deny) on the three builders; extend the builder source test

## Expected impact
Closes a popup path out of the app origin if one exists; nothing changes if Tauri already denies by default. Could break a feature relying on window.open (grep shows none).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - no webview can open an unguarded window
Before: unknown: the default was not observed in this round
After: popups refused on 3 of 3 windows, pinned by a source test
Method: simulation - needs a running app to observe the default; no dev run allowed in a round
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: debug run: window.open('https://example.com') from each window's devtools, Before vs After; source test that every builder chain has on_new_window

title: Bring window-duality's Tumbler capability example in line with the generated file
body:
## Summary
docs/design/window-duality.md and its HTML show the Tumbler capability holding core:default and core:window:allow-start-dragging; the generated file holds neither.

## Description
docs/design/window-duality.md:277 and docs/design/window-duality.html:992 list "core:default", "core:window:allow-start-dragging" for the Tumbler. apps/desktop/src-tauri/tests/capabilities.rs forbids core:default, and commit ff5738c dropped start-dragging; capabilities/tumbler.json grants core:event:allow-listen/unlisten plus allow-<command> rows only. AGENTS names window-duality a source of truth, so a reader copying the example would widen the Tumbler. Fixed: replace the example with the current generated content (or a pointer to it) in md and html together.

## Flow
- grep the doc's permission example
- compare with capabilities/tumbler.json
- edit md + html together

## Expected impact
Readers stop copying a wider grant than the app uses. Docs only.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the design doc states the grants the code enforces
Before: 2 permissions in the doc example that the generated file does not grant
After: 0
Method: probe - grep doc vs generated file; docs/ is outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Drop the debug-only loopback navigation allowance that no config uses
body:
## Summary
Debug builds let every webview navigate to any port on localhost/127.0.0.1/[::1], but the app never loads from a dev server.

## Description
apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/native/navigation.rs:16 allows http(s) loopback on any port when cfg!(debug_assertions); navigation_tests.rs:79-85 pins it. tauri.conf.json has no build.devUrl and scripts/dev/tauri-dev-test.mjs runs cargo run with the embedded dist, so the allowance has 0 users while any local service is reachable from a debug webview. Removing it narrows debug builds, but it is the owner's deliberate dev affordance, so the call is theirs (direction).

## Flow
- debug build: a webview navigates to http://127.0.0.1:<any>/ -> allowed
- release build: refused (unchanged)
- fix: delete the loopback arm and flip loopback_dev_server_is_debug_only to refuse

## Expected impact
Debug builds stop reaching local services from the app windows; no release change. Breaks a future dev-server workflow until devUrl is added with its own rule.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - debug navigation matches what the app loads
Before: any loopback port navigable in debug, 0 configured users (grep devUrl: 0)
After: app origin only
Method: probe - grep for devUrl / dev server in config and scripts
Result: better
Gate: direction
instrument: navigation_tests: loopback refused with dev=true; grep devUrl in tauri.conf.json and scripts -> 0
